_comments: Orders: Generate Invoice.
GenerationType is effectively Manual here — Type=Custom, so nothing is AI-generated and the
DriverClass points at a hand-authored subclass in packages/Actions. The registration key is
namespaced ('Orders.GenerateInvoice') for the same reason the remote operations are: 'Generate
Invoice' is a name another Open App will eventually want, and the ClassFactory resolves by
string.
AN ORDER CAN PRODUCE MORE THAN ONE DOCUMENT. Lines sold by different companies are different
receivables owed to different legal entities, so the action returns an ARRAY and the scalar
HTML output is null whenever it split. A caller that reads HTML and ignores DocumentCount gets
nothing rather than half a bill presented as the whole one.
IT WRITES NOTHING. There is no invoice record — the confirmed order is the receivable — so this
is safe to call repeatedly, from a workflow, an agent, or a print button.

fields.Name: Generate Invoice
fields.Description: Render an order as the document you send a customer: an invoice, a quote (for a draft or quoted order) or a credit memo (for a reversal). Returns self-contained HTML ready for a PDF renderer or an email body, plus the underlying figures so a caller can reconcile without parsing markup. Writes nothing. An order sold by more than one company produces one document per company, each billing only what that company is owed.
fields.UserPrompt: Given an order, produce the customer-facing document for it using the 'Orders: Standard Invoice' template.

fields.Name: OrderID
fields.Description: The order to render. Any status except Voided — a voided order is refused rather than rendered, because a bill for money nobody owes is indistinguishable from a real one once it is a PDF in an inbox.

fields.Name: CompanyID
fields.Description: Render only the document for this selling company. Omit to get every document the order produces. Narrowing does not renumber the others: the -A/-B suffix describes the order, not the size of the result.

fields.Name: AsOfDate
fields.Description: The date the document is produced (YYYY-MM-DD). Drives the days-until-due countdown and the generated-on line, nothing else — the figures come from the order and do not move. Defaults to today.

fields.Name: TemplateName
fields.Description: The MJ Template to render. A deployment can point this at its own template without forking the code — that is the reason the markup lives in the database at all.

fields.Name: Locale
fields.Description: BCP 47 tag driving number grouping and date order.

fields.Name: CurrencyCode
fields.Description: Override the currency. By default each document uses its SELLING COMPANY's functional currency from the accounting profile, which is where the fact actually lives — currency is a property of the seller, not of the sale.

fields.Name: Format
fields.Description: 'HTML' renders the document; 'DATA' returns the figures alone and skips the template entirely, for callers reconciling rather than sending. PDF is produced by handing the HTML to a renderer — this action does not shell out to one.

fields.Name: ShowDiagnostics
fields.Description: Print the internal notes block on the document — money the builder had to place by judgement rather than by allocation, and any ladder that failed to reach its own total. For checking a document, never for sending one.

fields.Name: Invoices
fields.Description: One entry per document: DocumentNumber, Kind, CompanyID, CompanyName, Gross, AmountDue, HTML and the full decorated figures under Data. This is the authoritative output; the scalar HTML below is only a convenience.

fields.Name: HTML
fields.Description: The rendered document, for the overwhelmingly common single-company order. NULL when the order produced more than one — handing back the first of two as though it were the whole bill is the failure this deliberately refuses.

fields.Name: DocumentCount
fields.Description: How many documents this order produced. Greater than one means the order was split by selling company, and the ResultCode says SPLIT_BY_COMPANY.

fields.Name: Notes
fields.Description: Anything the builder decided rather than read, prefixed with the document it belongs to. Empty is the expected state; a non-empty list is worth a look before the document goes out.

_comments: Orders: Send Document — the irreversible twin of Generate Invoice.
SEPARATE FROM GENERATE INVOICE ON PURPOSE. Generating writes nothing and is safe to call a
hundred times; sending reaches a person outside the company and cannot be undone. A `Send: true`
flag on the render action would put this app's most consequential side effect behind a boolean
that is easy to set by accident.
IT IS NOT IDEMPOTENT. Calling it twice sends the document twice. The Deliveries output carries an
IdempotencyKeys array per document so a caller that needs at-most-once can build its own guard —
this action cannot make that judgement, because re-sending at a customer's request is ordinary and
re-sending because a workflow retried is not.
AN ORDER SOLD BY TWO COMPANIES SENDS TWO DOCUMENTS, one per selling company, each billing only
what its company is owed. A partial failure returns PARTIALLY_SENT rather than failing the whole
call, so a retry does not re-send the ones that worked.

fields.Name: Send Document
fields.Description: Render an order as its customer-facing document and SEND it. Resolves the billing contacts the order names, refuses anything that is not a bill (a draft or a voided order), and delivers through the requested channel. Email today; the channel is a plugin seam. Set PreviewOnly to render and address the message without sending it.
fields.UserPrompt: Given an order, render its invoice and email it to the customer's billing contacts.

fields.Name: OrderID
fields.Description: The order to send. Any status except Draft, Voided or Cancelled — those render but are refused here, because a document that looks exactly like a real invoice must not reach a customer's inbox for money nobody owes.

fields.Name: CompanyID
fields.Description: Send only the document for this selling company. Omit to send every document the order produces.

fields.Name: Channel
fields.Description: How to send it. 'Email' today; the resolver refuses a code with no registered channel rather than silently doing nothing.

fields.Name: ToAddress
fields.Description: Override the recipients with a single address — for 'send me a copy'. Omit to use the billing contacts the order names. Naming an address IS the deliberate decision that recipient resolution otherwise requires.

fields.Name: CC
fields.Description: Additional recipients, comma- or semicolon-separated.

fields.Name: BCC
fields.Description: Blind recipients, comma- or semicolon-separated. Useful for an archive mailbox.

fields.Name: From
fields.Description: Sending address. Omit to let the communication provider use its configured sender — a guess here is either rejected by domain authentication or, worse, accepted and sends invoices from an address nobody monitors.

fields.Name: FromName
fields.Description: Display name for the sender.

fields.Name: TemplateName
fields.Description: Template to render. Defaults to 'Orders: Standard Invoice'.

fields.Name: Locale
fields.Description: Locale for dates and money on the rendered document. Defaults to en-US.

fields.Name: CurrencyCode
fields.Description: Overrides the selling company's functional currency. Only for a caller who genuinely knows better.

fields.Name: PreviewOnly
fields.Description: Render and address the message WITHOUT sending it. A channel must honour this — a preview that sends is invisible on the sending side.

fields.Name: Deliveries
fields.Description: One entry per document: its number, whether it was sent, the addresses that accepted it, the reason if not, and the idempotency keys for a caller doing its own de-duplication.

fields.Name: SentCount
fields.Description: How many documents went out.

fields.Name: FailedCount
fields.Description: How many did not. Non-zero means the result code is NOT_SENT or PARTIALLY_SENT.
